## Notes

### Quick read
- Tayler is a redheaded mom of three boys (school-age oldest, a toddler, and a baby boy) who films real outings in parking lots, Walmart, parks and a small-town parade, and she is one of our strongest earners ($4,160 GMV, 67 conversions, ROAS 1.6). PROTECTED: never message her about commission.
- Best next move: ask for more of her talking-to-camera wrap vs sling stories (Fatima's Aug 16 ask); the Sep 16 "waiting five minutes for my wrap" video is approved but not yet run as an ad, so worth pushing to the media buyer.

### Style (from watching her videos)
- Who she is on camera: mom of three boys, long wavy red hair, big black or red sunglasses, black tanks and denim, real errands energy. Setting is almost always out and about: Walmart parking lot and aisles, a playground, a town parade (Wyoming flag, horses), a dirt lot beside her SUV. Baby boy looks roughly 4 to 8 months across the videos. Uses the Checkered sling with the colourful mandala strap.
- Format: mix of (1) talking-to-camera storytime filmed selfie style (Walmart parking lot wrap panic, the five minute wrap wait), (2) text-overlay b-roll "day with three kids" montages, (3) a split-screen skit with two versions of herself (wrap vs sling). Relatable, a little frazzled then relieved, honest mom voice. Length 11 to 44s.
- Hooks (quote): "I could literally feel my anxiety rising as I stood in the Walmart parking lot watching a YouTube video trying to figure out how to put my wrap on"; "If you have more than one kid, you know park trips are basically a workout"; "One takes forever... the other takes seconds."; "Here's all the ways" (bathroom at Walmart, helping toddler wash hands, helping oldest shop for school, "Carrying a sleeping baby without the backache"); "When the Bambora sling is worth the hype and you can enjoy the parade with ALL your kids"; "Before finding Bambora, my family used to have to wait a solid five minutes for me to put on my wrap".
- What worked: all 6 videos approved. f8b61b37 (Walmart parking lot wrap anxiety talking head, "Amazing!") ran as 2 ads and is the video Fatima called "crushing" on Aug 9; 5db9a835 (park, back pain) 2 ads; 436487e5 (parade) 2 ads; a5fbc28c (split-screen wrap vs sling skit, "Such a good concept!") 1 ad; 344cc8e1 ("all the ways" Walmart montage to a trending "woman on a mission" sound) 1 ad. ef5d0847 (Sep 16) not run yet.
- The through-line: fabric wrap frustration vs a sling that buckles on in seconds, and keeping up with older kids. Her own story (used a wrap with her first two, hated it) makes this authentic.
- Safety and checklist issues seen:
  - f8b61b37 (running): transcript says "my hands are available", which leans on the retired hands free claim. It predates the guidelines, but new videos should use the arm and back relief framing instead.
  - 5db9a835 (running): climbs the playground steps with baby in the sling; the checklist says no stairs.
  - 344cc8e1 (running): while helping her toddler wash hands and helping her oldest try on clothes, no hand is visibly on the baby.
  - ef5d0847: selfie angle means the seat and hand are out of frame for most of it; at 38s baby's legs hang with one hand at his back. Fine but not a clear seat demo.
  - The split-screen skit has no baby in the sling at all (just the wrap vs sling putting-on race).
- Strengths to lean on: authentic storytelling, strong comparison angle, busy mom of three life, outdoors and in-store settings that feel real.
- To improve: keep one hand on baby while helping the older kids; avoid stairs and play structures; show the seat under the bottom once per video.
